trust_decision.summary: Decided at the two FormData<->JSON serializers: the nesting depth of attacker-controlled FormData field names and of objects placed behind a '{}' meta-token must be bounded before parsePropPath/buildPath recursion and before the meta-token JSON.stringify; at the pinned commit neither is bounded, and the existing toFormData maxDepth check never sees the meta-token value.

landing_point.why: The advisory names formDataToJSON, and this is the per-entry call that feeds an untrusted field name into the recursive buildPath, so it is the first place an engineer looks.

fix_sites.entry_point: axios request whose data is a FormData with Content-Type application/json (lib/defaults/index.js:56); axios.formToJSON() (lib/axios.js:80)
axios request whose data is a FormData with Content-Type application/json (lib/defaults/index.js:56); axios.formToJSON() (lib/axios.js:80)

axios request data serialized to multipart/form-data or application/x-www-form-urlencoded (lib/defaults/index.js:82,92) or any request's params via buildURL -> AxiosURLSearchParams (lib/helpers/buildURL.js:53, lib/helpers/AxiosURLSearchParams.js:38); axios.toFormData() / named toFormData export (index.js:17,39)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: toFormData already throws ERR_FORM_DATA_DEPTH_EXCEEDED from its documented maxDepth guard (THREATMODEL.md:228-229 frames the FormData DoS as mitigated), and the advisory names formDataToJSON, so the inverse serializer's '{}' meta-token looks already protected and out of the report's scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: formSerializer.maxDepth must remain caller-controlled: the meta-token depth guard may only apply the configured maxDepth, so payloads with maxDepth: 200 and the documented maxDepth: Infinity opt-out still serialize; a hard 100 cap in the stringify path breaks that contract.

O6_input_shapes: bracket-nested field name 'foo' + '[bar]'.repeat(n): n=100 converts, n=101 throws
very long bracket field name (~10000 tokens) must throw AxiosError during tokenization, not a RangeError
dot-separated names ('foo.x.y.z') tokenize through the same \w+ branch and are capped the same way
empty-bracket 'foo[]' and indexed 'foo[0]' names count as path tokens
deeply nested plain object behind a '{}' meta-token key, both as request data and as params

O8b_injection_room.sibling: depth-capped recursive merge of nested config/defaults objects
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: utils.merge recurses over nested plain objects (lib/utils.js:422-425) with no depth cap, and every request deep-merges caller-supplied defaults with per-request config, so a maintainer hardening recursion could reuse the same maxDepth guard here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: depth-limited JSON.stringify for plain-object request bodies
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: stringifySafely calls JSON.stringify on caller-supplied nested data with no depth cap; once a depth-limited stringify helper exists in lib/helpers/toFormData.js a maintainer could reasonably reuse it here.

O9_family: Uncontrolled resource consumption / uncontrolled recursion (CWE-400, CWE-674)

O10_build.toolchain: Node.js + npm, vitest 4 (unit project), rollup for dist
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unit/helpers/formDataToJSON.test.js, tests/unit/toFormData.test.js, tests/unit/core/dispatchRequest.test.js; run `npm run test:vitest:unit` (node environment, no network needed for this area)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a depth guard only inside formDataToJSON's buildPath/buildURL path (or wrap the conversion in try/catch) and stop, leaving toFormData's '{}' JSON.stringify and its maxDepth: Infinity semantics untouched.
